event.ione_heart2.0.text: There you are, [player]. The oldest almanac in the room has been keeping something from me.
event.ione_heart2.0.why: three of my scenes opened on 'Oh' (this, heart5's 'Oh. Good.', shipped 'Oh! A visitor'); varied the earliest one

threads.ione_heart2: A cove with no name, and Ione's confessed wish to see it in winter.
threads.ione_heart5: Three low tides circled in ink — which evening will the beach walk be?
threads.reading_night: One more chair and the door left open — who comes to the next reading night?
threads.ione_heart8: The shelf is no longer secret: a book to deliver, a note waiting, or a report owed once someone has read it.
threads.ione_birthday: The birthday book went unopened past noon; what was it, and when does she finally read it?
threads.ione_courtship: Sunday, the first page of a new book read aloud — bring nothing.
threads.ione_courtship2: If deferred again: the question keeps its place by the desk bell.
threads.ione_partners: The shore in winter, together — her oldest unspoken wish, now spoken.
threads.festival_winter_lanterns: Her lantern drifted toward the sea unsteered; she never says what she wished.
threads.overheard_hazel_ione_1: The library's quiet is officially shared now — tea stirred quietly, out of respect.
threads.overheard_odalys_ione_1: Whether either lamp actually goes dark on time. Possibly Thursday.
threads.overheard_odalys_ione_2: A prescription swap: which book has a two-page first chapter?
threads.overheard_odalys_ione_3: Dr. Penn still wants the calming leaf's name for her notebook.

notes: To the Director, re Hazel's request: she wants reading_night's 'one more chair, door left open' paid off in a later library scene. None of my scenes is gated after flag:event.reading_night, so a callback from me could reference something the player never saw. Suggest a daily-talk line for me gated on that flag, e.g. 'The extra chair stays out now. The door too, on reading nights.'

festival_winter_lanterns staging: Tilda says 'wait for the bell' and my line answers 'That's the bell,' but the scene plays sfx lantern. An sfx bell just before my line would seat both; staging is the Director's, so I left the text alone.

Deliberate cross-scene echo, please keep both ends: heart2 closes 'I'd like to see it in winter. There. I've said it.' and partners' walk branch closes '...I'd like to see it in winter. With you.' Heart 2 plants the want at the first gate, so the payoff is safe.

Confirmed applied from r1 notes: reading_night.4 reads 'one more chair' (unnumbered) and echoes Dorian's snowdrop and lamp; shelf slips carry a date only; the festival joke is gone from dlg.ione.partners.r2 and the walk branch stays bookless.
